messages.content: A certain tree was 100 meters tall at the end of 2017. It will grow 10% more than its previous height each year. How long has the tree grown from 2017 until the end of 2019?

At the end of 2017, the tree was 100 meters tall. Each year, it grows by 10% of its height at the end of the previous year.

At the end of 2018, the tree's height is 100 meters + 10% of 100 meters = 100 meters + 10 meters = 110 meters.

At the end of 2019, the tree's height is 110 meters + 10% of 110 meters = 110 meters + 11 meters = 121 meters.

The growth from 2017 to the end of 2019 is the difference between the height at the end of 2019 and the height at the end of 2017, which is 121 meters - 100 meters = 21 meters.

The tree has grown 21 meters from 2017 until the end of 2019.

FINAL: 21

Given:
- Initial height of the tree at the end of 2017: 100 meters
- Annual growth rate: 10%

Unknown:
- Total growth from the end of 2017 to the end of 2019

Operations:
1. Calculate the height at the end of 2018 by applying the 10% growth to the height at the end of 2017.
2. Calculate the height at the end of 2019 by applying the 10% growth to the height at the end of 2018.
3. Subtract the initial height from the height at the end of 2019 to find the total growth.

Step-by-step solution:
1. Height at the end of 2018: \(100 \text{ meters} + 10\% \times 100 \text{ meters} = 100 \text{ meters} + 10 \text{ meters} = 110 \text{ meters}\)
2. Height at the end of 2019: \(110 \text{ meters} + 10\% \times 110 \text{ meters} = 110 \text{ meters} + 11 \text{ meters} = 121 \text{ meters}\)
3. Total growth: \(121 \text{ meters} - 100 \text{ meters} = 21 \text{ meters}\)

Concrete check:
- Initial height: 100 meters
- Height at the end of 2018: 110 meters
- Height at the end of 2019: 121 meters
- Total growth: 21 meters

The total growth from the end of 2017 to the end of 2019 is 21 meters.

FINAL: 21
